question: According to the Europa Nostra technical report published on 19 September 2025, the cable car project in Monemvasia, Greece, has been included in measure 16735 of the Greek Recovery and Resilience Plan, which aims to ‘harness art as a prescribed therapy to promote social cohesion and activate the “silver economy”’.

The same report notes that this measure is not fully in line with the objectives of the initial project approval decisions and that there is no clear documentation to support the selection of this specific site.

The project is being carried out in a protected area (Natura 2000, Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty and a designated archaeological site), which is included in the Peloponnese Regional Spatial Planning Framework as a proposed candidate for inclusion in the UNESCO World Heritage List. Can the Commission say: 1.
To what extent does it consider the financing of the construction of a cable car in Monemvasia compatible with the content and objectives of measure 16735 of the Greek Recovery and Resilience Plan?

Has it examined whether the relevant requirements of Regulation (EU) 2021/241 on the Recovery and Resilience Facility are being met, in particular as regards compliance with EU law on environmental and cultural protection and the ‘do no significant harm’ principle?
Will it request additional clarifications or review the financing of the project should failings in the project’s appropriateness or approval process be identified?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (1.12.2025) Measure 16735 of the Greek Recovery and Resilience Plan (RRP) aims to improve physical access to cultural venues, including for older people and persons with disabilities.

According to Decision 185395 of 19 December 20221, the construction of the Monemvasia lift was integrated in the Greek RRP under measure 16735 to ensure access for persons with mobility constraints to the upper town of Monemvasia, to speed up access in case of an emergency, and to transfer materials for the preservation of monuments.

The Recovery and Resilience Facility (RRF) Regulation (EU) 2021/2412 provides that no measure included in a RRP should do significant harm to environmental objectives within the meaning of Article 17 of Regulation (EU) 2020/852 ‘do no significant harm’ (DNSH).

Decision 185395 of 19 December 2022 sets out that the installation of the lift should be carried out with due regard to the landscape and environment, and that the project should comply with Regulation (EU) 2021/241 including the DNSH principle. The published call for tender also requires that the project should comply with EU and national environmental and other rules3.

The siting of the project was approved, in accordance with archaeological legislation, by Decision 452351 of 23 September 2021 of the Minister of Culture following the unanimous opinion of the Central Archaeological Council. The RRF is a performance-based financing instrument.

Therefore, the Commission releases funds to Member States only after it has assessed the satisfactory fulfilment of the agreed milestones and targets that are linked to the reforms and investments under the RRP. At present, payment requests related to this measure have not been submitted by Greece and thus have not yet been assessed by the Commission.
